name: Pahranagat National Wildlife Refuge (Upper Lake Campground)
note: USFWS refuge with 15 primitive lakeside sites along Upper Pahranagat Lake off US-93 south of Alamo. First-come, first-served (donation box). No hookups or potable water; vault toilets, picnic tables, grills, fire pits. Ten sites (1, 2, 2a, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 12, 13) take larger RVs (some to ~30 ft); three are tent-only. 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Big Creek Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD), ~12 mi SW of Austin at the mouth of Big Creek Canyon via FS Rd 002. 8 FCFS sites, open mid-May-late Oct; no potable water, vault toilets, picnic tables. Fairly open setting; RVs to ~35 ft per FS/reviews but the access road is rough (high-clearance recommended; trailers barred from crossing the top of FSR 002 through-route). --Claude

name: Columbine Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD), small rustic campground at ~8,600 ft along Steward Creek on the west side of the Toiyabe Range, at the Columbine Trailhead into the Arc Dome Wilderness. 7 open sites, RVs/trailers to ~35 ft; first-come, first-served, no potable water, vault toilets. Reached via SR-722/Rte 21 and 10 mi of FS Rd 119 (graded dirt). --Claude

name: Hickison Petroglyphs Recreation Area Campground
note: BLM (Mount Lewis Field Office) primitive campground on US-50 ~24 mi E of Austin. ~16-20 drive-in sites with picnic tables, fire rings/BBQ grills and vault toilets; no water. First-come, first-served, open year-round, 14-day limit. Most sites suit vans/small trailers - larger rigs can maneuver but scout first. Short trail to petroglyphs. --Claude

name: Kingston Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Austin-Tonopah RD), 12 sites at ~7,100 ft along Kingston Creek in Kingston Canyon in the Toiyabe Range. First-come, first-served, open mid-May-late Oct; picnic tables, fire pits, vault toilets, no potable water. RVs to ~35 ft but the final 2.5-mi single-lane dirt road is tight for big rigs - scout sites on foot. --Claude

name: Baker Creek Campground (Great Basin National Park)
note: NPS Great Basin NP, ~3 mi down gravel Baker Creek Rd off the Lehman Caves entrance road. ~37 sites at ~7,500 ft; Lower Loop takes RVs/trailers (some sites to ~50 ft), Upper Loop (9-14) is no-RV. Reservable via recreation.gov Jun-early Aug, otherwise first-come, first-served (open ~mid-May-late Sep). Vault toilets, fire grills, no potable water. --Claude

name: Sacramento Pass Campground
note: BLM (Ely District) recreation area just off US-50 ~15 mi W of the Utah line and E of Great Basin NP. 10 large sites on an upper loop (4) and a lower loop (6 pull-thrus circling a small stocked pond); gravel spurs to ~60 ft, big-rig friendly. First-come, first-served, open year-round, 14-day limit; vault toilets, shade structures, no potable water. Dark skies. --Claude

name: Mill Creek Recreation Area
note: BLM Battle Mountain. 11 drive-in sites in a cottonwood-studded canyon, reached 4 mi off SR-305 on a maintained gravel road (~20 mi S of Battle Mountain); picnic tables, fire rings, pit toilets, no water or hookups. First-come first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Government Wash Campground
note: NPS Lake Mead NRA, near the west entrance from Las Vegas. Reopened Feb 2026 after a 2023-2025 restoration into ~50 defined campsites (NPS gives 47 and 51) on graded desert roads with fire rings and a small-boat/kayak ramp; no hookups, water, or permanent restrooms. Closed to vehicles and overnight camping until about late November 2026 (NPS, Oct 15 2026); hosts are not kept on site in the summer heat. 28-day stay limit, first-come first-served; no campsite fee posted, the park entrance fee applies. --Claude

name: Sheldon National Wildlife Refuge, Virgin Valley Campground
note: USFWS Sheldon NWR, ~25 mi W of Denio Junction. Drive-in campground ~2 mi off NV-140 on a maintained dirt road; designated RV/tent spaces, drinking water, vault toilets, tables, fire rings, plus a geothermal warm-springs pool and a rustic bathhouse with showers. 14-day limit, first-come first-served. --Claude

name: Jack Creek Campground
note: USFS Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, Mountain City-Ruby Mtns-Jarbidge RD. Small campground on the banks of Jack Creek below Jacks Peak; RVs to 25 ft, vault toilets, tables, fire rings, no water. Reached off paved roads via BLM/ranch gravel. First-come first-served, ~May-Nov. --Claude

name: Tabor Creek Campground
note: BLM Elko District, ~30 mi N of Wells via Upper Metropolis Rd (gravel). 10 primitive drive-in sites along Tabor Creek with tables, fire rings, vault toilets, and shade trees; no drinking water or hookups. First-come first-served, 14-day limit. --Claude

name: Wildhorse Crossing Campground
note: USFS Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, Mountain City-Ruby Mtns-Jarbidge RD. ~19 sites in the Owyhee River canyon on NV-225, ~68 mi N of Elko and just N of Wildhorse Reservoir; tables, fire rings/grills, vault toilets, trash, no water. Trailers/RVs to ~35 ft. First-come first-served, ~May-Nov (not on recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Illipah Reservoir Campground
note: BLM Ely District recreation area on Illipah Reservoir, ~37 mi west of Ely off US-50. ~15 sites suitable for large trailers and RVs; grills, tables, shade structures at most sites, vault toilets, no potable water. First-come first-served (not on recreation.gov). Trout fishing/boating; year-round. Elevation ~6,840 ft. --Claude

name: Kalamazoo Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Ely RD), small campground adjacent to Kalamazoo Creek on the east side of the Schell Creek Range. 8 sites with tables, fire rings, BBQ pedestals; no potable water. FCFS, not on recreation.gov. Per fs page accommodates full-sized RVs in dry weather, but the access road is bumpy/narrow and high-clearance/4WD is advised when wet. Open ~late May-mid Oct. --Claude

name: Wheeler Peak Campground
note: Great Basin NP alpine campground at ~9,900 ft at the end of the Wheeler Peak Scenic Drive; 37 standard non-hookup sites. Hard 24-ft max on both towing and towed vehicles (the scenic drive is narrow with an 8% grade and tight curves) - a compact 23-ft rig fits under the cap but only a subset of the small gravel sites accommodate one, and the NPS discourages larger trailers. Vault toilets, drinking water; reservable/FCFS in summer, road closed by snow otherwise. --Claude

name: Twenty Mile Beach Campground (Walker Lake)
note: BLM Walker Lake Recreation Area drive-in dispersed beach on the west shore off US-95, ~12 mi N of Hawthorne; northernmost of the area's three BLM camping beaches. Hard-packed sand/gravel and a graded access road near the entrance (looser sand nearer the water - stay high), vault toilet, no potable water. First-come, first-served, primitive fee. --Claude

name: Mount Rose Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF (Carson RD) campground at ~8,900 ft on the Mt. Rose Hwy (SR-431) between Reno and Lake Tahoe; single/double/one triple family sites, RVs to ~35 ft, no hookups, vault toilets and drinking water. First-come, first-served (some sites via recreation.gov). --Claude

name: Jarbidge Campground
note: Small primitive Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground at the historic town of Jarbidge (~6,350 ft) in Jarbidge Canyon, NE Nevada; a handful of sites best for small/medium rigs (~22-24 ft, comparable to nearby Sawmill), vault toilet, no potable water. First-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct once the canyon road clears. Reached via the long graded Jarbidge Canyon Rd - remote but passable by a normal vehicle. --Claude

name: Sawmill Campground
note: Small rustic Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground ~1 mi N of Jarbidge (~6,100 ft) in Jarbidge Canyon; 5 sites for small/medium vehicles, trailers/motorhomes to under ~25 ft (a 23-ft rig fits, tight), vault toilets, fire rings, no potable water. First-come, first-served, open ~June-Oct. Reached via graded Jarbidge Canyon Rd - remote but passable by a normal vehicle. --Claude

name: McWilliams Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, Spring Mountains NRA, Lee Canyon (Mount Charleston) ~40 mi from Las Vegas, ~8,500 ft. Largest campground in the NRA: 70+ single/double sites, no hookups, vault toilets. Sites fit RVs/trailers 20-64 ft. Odd sites reservable on recreation.gov, even sites FCFS; full campground open May-Oct, sites 1-14 year-round. --Claude

name: Hilltop Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, Spring Mountains NRA, upper Kyle Canyon (Mount Charleston) ~40 mi from Las Vegas, ~8,400 ft. 35 single/double sites, no hookups, no potable water, vault toilets, paved spurs. Trailers over 25 ft not recommended due to tight turns (23-ft rig OK). Odd sites reservable on recreation.gov, even sites FCFS; open May-Nov. --Claude

name: Echo Bay Campground
note: NPS Lake Mead NRA, Overton Arm, ~10 mi S of the Northshore entrance. Paved sites for tents/RVs, no hookups; dump station and water fill near the Upper Campground entrance, restrooms and water spigots throughout, no showers. Lower loop (sites 1-34) reservable on recreation.gov, Upper Campground FCFS (~112 sites); open year-round. --Claude

name: South Ruby Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground above Ruby Lake at the base of the Ruby Mountains, adjacent to Ruby Lake NWR, ~1,860 m (6,000 ft). 35 sites (33 single, 1 double, 1 accessible), vault toilets, tables, fire rings, seasonal drinking water; no hookups. Reservable on recreation.gov Memorial Day-Labor Day, lower loop FCFS off-season. Access via graded gravel county roads (drive-in). --Claude

name: Wilson Canyon Recreation Area (BLM)
note: BLM (Carson City District) multi-use recreation area along the West Walker River, ~13 mi west of Yerington off paved SR-208 (turn onto Copperbelt Dr, ~0.5 mi dirt). No designated sites — RVs/trailers overnight in the drive-in staging areas near the river; vault toilet nearby, no water. 14-day limit; FCFS dispersed. Also an OHV/staging area. --Claude

name: Angel Lake Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground at Angel Lake in the East Humboldt Range, ~12 mi SW of Wells via the paved NV-231 scenic byway, ~2,550 m (8,400 ft). ~25-26 single/double sites (some with lake views), tables, fire rings, vault toilets, no potable water/hookups; rec.gov lists RV sites. Reservable on recreation.gov Memorial Day-Labor Day, some FCFS. Access road is paved but steep/switchbacked — a haul for larger rigs. --Claude

name: Pioche City RV Park
note: Town-operated RV park at 185 4th Street, Pioche (across from the City Park), Lincoln County. 10 pull-through sites, RVs only (no tents), shared water & dump/sewer; 7-day stay limit; donations requested. Open year-round, first-come, first-served. --Claude

name: Davis Creek Regional Park Campground
note: Washoe County regional park campground at 25 Davis Creek Rd, Washoe Valley, in the pines against Slide Mountain ~20 mi south of Reno off US-395. 62 sites in loops through pine/sage forest; NO hookups; 19 sites (21-39) fit travel trailers to 32 ft; dump station ($5), coin showers. Sites 2-30 & 35-60 reservable 15-180 days ahead via Washoe County Park Reservations (775-823-6501 / reserveparks@washoecounty.gov); FCFS inside 14 days. NOTE: tentatively CLOSED for the 2026 season due to major infrastructure damage from the Sept 2024 Davis Fire - confirm reopening with the county before planning a stay. --Claude

name: Pony Express RV Stop
note: Small no-frills transient RV stop on the east end of Austin (US-50, the 'Loneliest Road'), next to Austin City Park. 7 gravel pull-through sites, full hookups incl 50 amp. No showers/laundry on site; self-serve pay-envelope drop box (first-come, first-served / self-registration). Camper-reported rate: $45 a night (Campendium, July 2024). --Claude

name: Kyle Canyon Campground
note: USFS campground in the Spring Mountains NRA (Mount Charleston), Humboldt-Toiyabe NF, ~6,900 ft in timber. 27 sites (incl. 8 double + 1 triple); drinking water, vault restrooms, no hookups/showers. Roomy sites accommodate RVs. First-come, first-served -- not on recreation.gov. $12 Mon-Thu / $18 Fri-Sun. --Claude

name: Snowbird Mesa (Poverty Flats) Dispersed
note: BLM dispersed boondocking area (a.k.a. Poverty Flats) on the mesa off SR-169 between Overton and Lake Mead. Large flat gravel/dirt pads popular with big-rig snowbirds; no hookups or services, 14-day limit. Drive-in via gravel road up the mesa. First-come, first-served -- not on recreation.gov. --Claude

name: Pyramid Lake Dry Camping
note: Tribal permit drive-on-beach lakeside dry camping around Pyramid Lake (Pyramid Lake Paiute Tribe), near Sutcliffe/marina. No hookups; several beaches (Marina, Pelican Point, North Nets, Warrior Point) have vault toilets and trash removal. Daily/3-day camping permit required, bought online or at the Sutcliffe Ranger Station (2500 Lakeview Dr); no site reservations -- first-come, first-served dispersed. RVs regularly dry-camp on the accessible beaches; some soft-sand areas so check access. --Claude

name: Angel Creek Campground
note: Humboldt-Toiyabe NF campground in the East Humboldt/Ruby Mtns foothills ~8 mi SW of Wells at ~6,650 ft, in aspen groves along Angel Creek. 18 standard nonelectric sites plus a tent-only group area; vault toilets and drinking water, picnic tables and fire rings. Some sites reservable on recreation.gov (Memorial Day-Labor Day), remainder first-come, first-served; site 018 lists max RV 40 ft (many sites 35 ft). NOT a private/commercial park -- USFS-operated (RV Life mis-tagged commercial). --Claude

name: Cottonwood Campground (Canyon de Chelly National Monument)
note: Campground at Canyon de Chelly NM (NPS unit on Navajo land; run by the Navajo Nation Tseyi' Dine Heritage Area), ~93 sites, no hookups, water and flush toilets, dump station on exit. First-come, first-served for individual sites (group sites reservable); cash-drop fee. Open roughly Apr-Oct. Drive-in sites fit RVs. --Claude

name: Lees Ferry Campground (Glen Canyon NRA)
note: NPS campground on a sage-covered bench above the Colorado River at Lees Ferry, 54 sites, no hookups, dump station, potable water, flush toilets; each site has a shade shelter, table and grill. First-come, first-served, ~$26/night. Sites fit RVs (listed to ~30 ft, some to 38 ft) so a 23-ft rig is fine. Boat launch ~2 mi. --Claude

name: Tusayan - Montane Campground (formerly Ten-X, Kaibab National Forest)
note: USFS campground (renamed from Ten-X) in the Kaibab NF ponderosa forest ~2 mi south of Tusayan/Grand Canyon, ~70 sites, no hookups, no on-site water fill; vault toilets. Pull-through sites accommodate up to 35 ft and back-in/parallel sites up to 34-38 ft, so a 23-ft rig fits. Reservable on Recreation.gov with some FCFS. --Claude

name: Burro Creek Campground
note: BLM Kingman Field Office campground on a bench above Burro Creek, ~1.5 mi off US-93 (paved access) ~1 mi S of Burro Creek Bridge. 23 individual sites + 1 group + 2 day-use; no hookups, flush toilets, drinking water, dump station. Sites 1, 2 and 10-17 best for larger Class A/fifth-wheels. Group and sites 7,9,10-17 reservable online, rest FCFS. --Claude

name: Beehives Campground
note: NPS primitive campground in Glen Canyon NRA on a Navajo-sandstone bench across US-89 from Wahweap, near Page. ~21 gravel pull-out sites; no hookups, no water, no dump, no trash (pack out; bring portable toilet); $14/night, FCFS, 3-night limit. Pads fit rigs to ~25 ft (larger use Wahweap). Beehive Trail leads to Wahweap Bay overlooks. --Claude

name: Painted Rock Petroglyph Campground
note: BLM Lower Sonoran Field Office campground beside the Painted Rock petroglyph site, ~12.5 mi W of Gila Bend off I-8 (Exit 102) then ~11 mi N. 59 individual sites + 2 group; no water/electric hookups, vault toilets, trash. Hardened dirt/gravel roads suited to larger Class A/fifth-wheels when dry; all FCFS. --Claude

name: Bonito Campground, Coconino National Forest
note: Coconino NF (Flagstaff RD) campground at the entrance to Sunset Crater Volcano NM, ~12 mi NE of Flagstaff via US-89 and FR-545, ~6,900 ft in ponderosa pine over old lava flows. 44 single sites (22 reservable / 22 FCFS); no hookups, paved roads and spurs, drinking water, flush toilets. Motorhomes/trailers over 42 ft not permitted, so a 23-ft rig fits easily. --Claude
